text:
Samir: Hey team, customer reported a billing delta: their SDK estimator shows ~2.6k tokens for a session but invoice shows ~10.4k. They only made a single user request via streaming. Can someone help triage? I attached their curl repro below.

Devon: Can you paste the exact curl they used and whether they were using our JS/Go SDK or a raw streaming call? :eyes:

Samir: Raw streaming curl (redacted API key):

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-1","stream":true,"input":"Summarize the docs..."}' \  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
```

They also showed intermittent network flakiness (mobile client). The SDK estimate (local tokenization) is ~2.6k. Invoice line items show two completion events for that session totaling ~10.4k (i.e. ~4x).

Devon: A couple of things to check: 1) were there reconnects? 2) did they see partial outputs locally? 3) any identical request IDs in their logs?

Samir: They confirmed the client retried twice (connection dropped, then client reconnected) and said final output looked normal (one final completion). Their client logs include the same X-Client-Request-Id value for both connections. They sent this abbreviated server trace (redacted):

```
[stream] request_id=abc-123 connect=start
[stream] request_id=abc-123 send: chunk-1
[stream] request_id=abc-123 disconnect: network
[stream] request_id=abc-123 connect=start (retry)
[stream] request_id=abc-123 send: chunk-2 (resume)
[stream] request_id=abc-123 completion: content-length=2600 tokens
[billing] meter:event completion request_id=abc-123 tokens=2600
[billing] meter:event completion request_id=abc-123 tokens=2600 <-- duplicate
[billing] invoice:agg request_id=abc-123 tokens_total=5200
```

Helen: From billing view I can confirm invoice shows two completion meter events for that request_id. Looks like the service emitted duplicate meter events when the same request_id reconnected. I'll tentatively provision a credit while we root cause.

Luis: Thanks @Samir @Devon. This is helpful. Quick summary of root cause we found in a separate runtime trace: when a streaming connection reconnects with the same client-provided request_id but without a resume token header, the runtime previously treated the new socket as a fresh completion stream and emitted a completion meter event for both the aborted stream (server-side partial) and the resumed final stream. Metering should dedupe by idempotency key + finalization flag, but our older code path didn't mark the aborted partial as non-billable in all cases.

Devon: So the customer saw only one final output, but the server already accounted a partial chunk as a completion meter event before the reconnect? That explains the ~2x. But their invoice was ~4x — any clue on why it's 4x not 2x?

Luis: The 4x comes from two factors: (1) the client retried twice (3 sockets total: initial, retry1, retry2) and (2) each aborted socket sometimes triggered both a partial "completion" event and a standalone "kv-cache-flush" event that was billed as model tokens in older meter schema. So 3 completion-like events + 1 cache-flush event ~= ~4x the final token count. We're patching to: dedupe completion events by request_id + session_epoch, and ensure cache-flush events are attributed separately (not double-counting model tokens).

Samir: What's the mitigation we can tell the customer now? They need something actionable quickly.

Luis: Short term: ask the customer to upgrade to SDK v2.4.1 which adds a resume-token header on reconnects and sets an ephemeral session epoch so the runtime can associate chunks correctly. If they cannot upgrade immediately, we can apply a server-side backfill that scans invoice meter events for obvious retry-duplicates in the last 7 days and issue provisional credits.

Helen: I'll create a provisional credit for the affected invoice and mark it as pending change. Please send me the CSV of affected request_ids and invoice ids. I'll route to finance for formal adjustment. :white_check_mark:

repro-bot: repro run triggered by Samir (2812345678). Attached sanitized trace and a minimal curl that reproduces the duplicate meter events when artificially dropping the socket after the first chunk.

Devon: For DEV/QA: quick repro steps for eng-runtime: 1) run the stream endpoint locally 2) open a socket, send initial user chunk, then close socket immediately 3) reconnect with same request_id but without resume token 4) observe two completion meter events emitted to billing queue. I pushed a unit test to internal PR 5427 to cover the dedupe logic. :shipit:

Samir: Thanks all. I shared the temporary workaround with the customer (upgrade SDK or share request_ids for credit). I'll follow up when Helen confirms the credit. Appreciated. :pray:
